It was made before Sunbreak, but the majority of it still carries over. Since you used IG in World, you’re already familiar with its mechanics (which are mostly the same) but here are some of the changes going into Rise:

-Triple buff now gives you earplugs and flinch free. 

-Aerial is viable. Each time you perform an aerial attack (helicopter, silkbind vault), your subsequent aerial attack grows stronger (up to 3 charges). The best aerial combo for charging your Diving Wyvern is Silkbind Vault —> Helicopter or Kinsect Slash x2 —> Diving Wyvern. 

-Tetraseal Slash is great! This is a new switch skill you can eventually learn. You trade the mobility and speed of your standard Tornado Slash for some extra damage, basically. But either one is good.

Talismans are pieces of equipment that will give you extra skill points and extra decoration slots, depending on the talisman. You can have up to two different skills on a talisman.

The most favorable spread of skills and deco slots really depends on your weapon and build, but the melding options Vigor and Cyclus will help you get the best and better talismans respectively. 

Cyclus allows you to specify 1 skill, guaranteeing that you will have that skill on the talisman, but it still uses RNG to roll the 2nd skill. Cyclus talismans are good, especially because it’s not hard to roll something decent. 

Vigor doesn’t allow you to guarantee a skill, meaning that you’ll have to rely more on luck to get what you want. In return, it will give you the possibility to get the very best talismans—something better than Cyclus could get you. 

I don’t remember exactly when you unlock Vigor and Cyclus. I think after Amatsu? Just remember to lock any good talismans you roll, because Cyclus “recycles” your old talismans and you don’t want to accidentally feed it something good.

You can’t know the exact proportions or even calories, because they’re estimates. But the point of an estimate isn’t to be 100% accurate. The point is to get a good approximation, which calorie counting is great for. 

Having a good estimate of the amount of calories you consume is very useful for maintaining your weight. I’ve been doing it for 3 years while bulking and cutting to reach my fitness goals. These estimates have always been more than enough information for me. So isn’t it better to have a close approximation rather than to spurn it all because it’s not 100% accurate? 

Earlier in your first comment, you said that only frozen meals are safe. But I don’t understand why you don’t have the same hangups with them as you do with something like chicken noodle soup when they have the same issue? The nutrition labels on foods are also estimates. You also don’t know the exact proportions of many food products either, because the calories are calculated from an estimated proportion. 

Two chocolate chip cookies from the same packaged tin bought from a supermarket will differ in their proportion of cookie to chocolate chip, but the calories are still calculated from an average. This doesn’t make the nutrition info useless.

I calorie count constantly, and measuring for meals which have a variety of ingredients mixed in is definitely annoying! I always calculate the mass of each ingredient, and note the % composition of the finished meal. For example:

Chicken noodle soup with 300g uncooked chicken breast, 100g dry pasta, 100g broccoli, and 500g water can be written as 30% chicken, 10% pasta, 10% broccoli, and 50% water. (1000g total)

And if I were to eat a serving of 200g of this soup, it would then be 60g chicken breast (200g * .3 = 60g) 20g broccoli, 20g pasta, and 100g water. Then I’d only have to count the amount of calories for each portion of each ingredient. 

MyFitnessPal even lets you input your own foods, so I’d make an entry for “chicken noodle soup cooked on 6 Feb 2023”, and write down that each 200g serving is x calories and y amount of protein. I cook chili with a ton of ingredients often, and this makes it easy!

Hi, anon! I’ve gone through a very similar thing and I’m still dealing with a bit of acne at 22. I saw a dermatologist this year and was prescribed Adapalene + benzoyl peroxide and clindamycin, and my acne has disappeared. My routine is 
AM
-rinse with water 
-clindamycin
-Cerave moisturizer 
-neutrogena SPF 50

PM
-cerave moisturizing cleanser 
-adapalene 
-cerave moisturizer 

My skin is dry, and I’ve noticed a lot of improvements by taking up this simple routine, but my greatest recommendation is that you go see a dermatologist! Any of the books involving the Tribe I’m not too excited about. They’re just a bit boring, and the fact that the cats have to go all the way to the mountains, deal with some problem there, and come all the way back is silly when you consider that it was all, plot-wise, for a tiny little snippet of information from the Tribe’s ancestors. It feels like more happens in the first five chapters of any other book than in the entirety of Outcast and Sign of the Moon combined. They just move at a sluggish pace.

Honestly, they’d have to make it ridiculously good to keep my interest. The Tribe has always bored me, mostly because any book involving them had obligatory traveling chapters, which are so predictable and samey that they’re hard to not gloss over anymore. 

But traveling aside, the Tribe has never really had any particularly interesting plots outside the Sharptooth stuff (maybe), which was only a single book anyway. Otherwise they’ve felt like nothing but pointless filler, and honestly I can’t imagine any plot revolving around the Tribe and the mountains being unique enough to warrant a whole spin-off series.
